gen-gf-turret-road-fs-gambetta: Turret Road comes in bold and commanding, its round forms bending like open parentheses in a pen-like line with no hairlines at all. Gambetta underneath swells and thins gently, and the text keeps moving.
gen-gf-turret-road-lora: Commanding and loud, Turret Road draws every letter like bent pipe cleaner, one steady line throughout. Lora follows with sturdy hairlines and a broad, welcoming c, so even a small heading would still hold its own against it.
gen-gf-underdog-fs-gambetta: Gambetta reads graceful and bookish, its wide channels leading into each counter while the strokes swell and taper gently. Underdog's horseshoe c and measured strokes make the contrast.
gen-gf-underdog-lora: Expressive and commanding, Underdog looks stitched. Its strokes are plain as thread outline, while Lora swings mellowly from thick to thin underneath, giving the page a loud voice and a gentler one.
gen-gf-unkempt-fs-gambetta: Unkempt scrawls its headings with no calligraphic shading, a t whose crossbar and stem match, and gaps that keep c from turning into o. Gambetta then takes over with modest thick-thin contrast, and Unkempt earns its keep big and short.
gen-gf-unkempt-lora: A pencil-line consistency runs through Unkempt, where the t's crossbar and stem match and every c stays clearly open, unlike a closed o. Lora adds modest stress in the curves.
gen-luckiest-guy-fs-bespoke-slab: Loud, cheerful and poured, Luckiest Guy sets its mean line high and gives o a ring with one constant wall. Bespoke Slab stays low and grounded.
gen-nixie-one-fs-gambetta: Gambetta reads bookish and graceful, with horizontal strokes slightly slimmer than the vertical ones and wide channels into each counter. Nixie One, retro-tech and unpinched, does the headline work, while Gambetta carries the reading.
gen-nixie-one-lora: Lora brings a literary, bookish voice with a broad, welcoming c and moderate thick-thin modulation. Nixie One, nostalgic and retro-tech, has no calligraphic thinning, and that contrast between the two is their strongest quality.
gen-silkscreen-fs-gambetta: Gambetta leads the eye with thick strokes that never dominate, graceful and bookish in feel. And Silkscreen, lo-fi and spaced out with a spaghetti line, gives that a retro foil.
